newsitem.title: FINLAND: BANKS EXPECT FINNISH MARKKA TO REMAIN VOLATILE.
newsitem.headline: BANKS EXPECT FINNISH MARKKA TO REMAIN VOLATILE.

text.p: The Finnish markka is expected to remain volatile and torn between conflicting interests in the near and medium term, two big Nordic banks said in their weekly market reports on Monday.
"We expect the markka to remain volatile as there are still significant foreign markka positions in the market," Finland's biggest banking group Merita Oy said.
Last week, talk of foreign investors unwinding markka positions led to a softening versus the German mark after the currency appreciated sharply the week before, Merita said.
Danish Unibank saw the markka firming medium term.
"The overall negative sentiment surrounding the Scandinavian currencies has caused an erosion of the markka over the past few days," it said.
"Longer out, we believe that the sharp movements in the Norwegian and Swedish crowns will be replaced by a positive trend and ... we look for markka appreciation," Unibank said.
It recommended buying markka against the German mark at 2.9985, set the stop-profit level of 2.9500 and the stop-loss level at 3.0250.
Early on Monday it traded slightly firmer than Friday's close, around 2.9925/mark.
Merita said DEM/FIM levels below 2.99 had triggered markka selling while levels above 3.00 had attracted buyers.
Both banks also warned of volatility due to EMU. --Helsinki newsroom +358-9-680 50 245, e-mail news@reuters.fi
